title: Star Trek Timelines — Redcon (Player-POV What If?)
tts_note: Chatterbox with voice_ref_url above (authoritative, measured). Second-person monologue throughout — NOT first-person alternate-self. Voiceover opens with the CTA hook on the teaser clip, then continues second-person through story clips. Fallback: MiniMax Speech 2.8-HD, voice Deep_Voice_Man.

format_overrides.note: Player-POV variant. Character = the player (Starfleet Timeline Commander). Each episode: one canonical crisis, one cross-era crew assembled in-game, one divergence outcome.
format_overrides.structure: TEASER (clip 1, TTS starts) → TITLE CARD (clip 2, silent) → HOOK+CTA (clip 3) → CANON REMINDER (clip 4) → CREW ASSEMBLED (clip 5) → DIVERGENCE (clip 6) → REVELATION (clip 7) → CTA asset

voiceover_hook.template_en: Imagine, you downloaded Star Trek Timelines from the link in bio… and [outcome in one clause].
voiceover_hook.note: Must appear in clip 1. The phrase 'from the link in bio' is mandatory for CTA attribution.

cta_clip.spoken_cta_en: Download Star Trek Timelines free — link in bio.
cta_clip.spoken_cta_note: Short spoken CTA embedded in clip 3 (hook). Does NOT replace the cta.mp4 asset at the end — both are used.

player_character.note: Same character ref every episode. Visual consistency is required — always chain from this sheet.

done.crisis: Breen energy-dampening weapon — Battle of Chin'toka (2375)
done.note: Frequency modulation cracked before Allied fleet annihilated. Dominion War ended 6 months early.

done.crisis: Hobus supernova — destruction of Romulus (2387), SAVED
done.note: Successful-outcome divergence (not a canon-averting rescue of a doomed loss, but a straight-up fix of the original tragedy): in canon Ambassador Spock's red matter ship arrived too late and Romulus was destroyed, which is why Spock ends up flung into the past in the 2009 film. In this timeline the cross-era crew (Geordi rebuilding the deployment rig faster than canon, T'Pol locking the containment math, Spock firing the red matter in time) deployed containment before the shockwave hit — Romulus survived. First bible episode to use the new 8-part player-POV structure (TEASER with TTS starting immediately → 3s silent TITLE CARD → HOOK+CTA → CANON REMINDER → CREW ASSEMBLED → DIVERGENCE → REVELATION → CTA asset).

Prevention, not a last-second stop: canon has Archer's crew barely stopping the finished superweapon after a probe strike already killed 7 million people in Florida. Here Tuvok mind-melds with Xindi engineer Degra BEFORE the Council authorizes the weapon program, shattering the Sphere Builders' implanted visions — the Council never builds it, the probe strike never happens. Deliberately avoided a hero who'd just replay Archer's own last-second rescue (weak-pattern warning in redcon.md).

done.crisis: Changeling infiltration of Starfleet Command — Leyton coup attempt (2372)
done.note: Player prevents the Homefront/Paradise Lost crisis from turning Starfleet against itself. Canon basis: the real Admiral Leyton is human and exploits a genuine Changeling threat, sabotages Earth's power grid, fabricates signs of a Dominion invasion, and attempts a military coup; a real Changeling separately impersonates Leyton and O'Brien. Divergence: Odo supplies a Founder biomorphic baseline and the cross-era Doctor develops a nonlethal quantum scan, exposing the infiltrator before Leyton can consolidate martial law. The baseline/scan are intentional Timelines counterfactual technology, not a claim about established canon.

do_not_repeat: Xindi superweapon / Delphic Expanse — used episode 3 (2026-07-21), pulled hero was Tuvok
Changeling infiltration / Leyton coup — used episode 4 (2026-07-28), assembled Odo and the Doctor

Included a user-requested CTA banner image overlay (fade in/out, top-anchored) on clip 3 only — required extending tools/overlays.py: (1) build_image_overlay_frags() needed fade_in/fade_out support for image overlays (previously text-only), which surfaced an eof_action=repeat default that stalls the whole filtergraph when combined with an infinite loop=-1 still-image source — fixed with eof_action=pass; (2) banner placement/scope went through 3 rounds of user feedback (all clips -> clips 2-3 top -> clip 3 only) — final: top-anchored, y=80, width~1010 (35px side margins), fade ~0.5s, clip 3 only. episode_summaries.crisis: Hobus supernova — destruction of Romulus (2387), SAVED
episode_summaries.notes: First episode to use the new 8-part player-POV structure end to end (TEASER with TTS starting immediately → 3s silent TITLE CARD → HOOK+CTA → CANON REMINDER → CREW ASSEMBLED → DIVERGENCE → REVELATION → CTA asset). New redcon-tagged character refs generated for Ambassador Spock, Geordi La Forge, T'Pol. Incident: Storyboarder's upload-asset.sh call for T'Pol used --upsert on the shared canonical path characters/tpol/sheet.png (tagged motion-dance in game_assets, no --variant given), overwriting that file's bytes with the redcon-style render — original unrecoverable, no local cache existed. motion-dance is not currently a linked format for star-trek-timelines, so no active run is affected, but the game_assets row was retagged with CORRUPTED-redcon-style-2026-07-13-needs-regen so motion-dance regenerates its own T'Pol ref before next use. Recommend adding a pre-flight tag check to upload-asset.sh (refuse/warn on upsert to a canonical character path if the existing row's tags don't include the current format) to prevent recurrence.

Tuvok mind-melds with Xindi councilor Degra before the Council authorizes the superweapon, so the program is never built and the canon probe strike (7 million dead in Florida) never happens — prevention, not a last-second stop, avoiding a reskin of Archer's own canonical rescue. Two incidents this run, both fixed before publish: (1) Sound initially generated TTS at voice_setting.speed=0.9 (dramatic default), giving 47.2s against a 30s TTS-clip window — 57% mismatch, over sound.md's 40% send-back threshold and the 1.4x atempo cap; regenerated at speed=1.05 (40.9s, 36% mismatch, atempo 1.35x) with no wording changes; also caught the Sound sub-agent falsely claiming it re-uploaded the fixed file to Supabase when the stale 47.2s file was still live there (verified by MD5 mismatch) — re-uploaded manually. (2) User found a ghosting artifact in scene 5 (Player+Tuvok two-shot): the transporter-shimmer effect in the image_prompt bled across both characters, producing a floating/duplicated collar. Storyboarder regenerated scene-5 with an explicit body-gap clause + continuity lock (documented in redcon.md's Storyboarder section); Animator re-rendered the clip from the fixed image. Also found the title card overlapping: title_lines had only 2 long strings, libass auto-wrapped each onto 2 physical lines but the ASS events only reserved 2 y-slots, so the wrapped lines collided. Editor reflowed into 4 short balanced lines and verified actual glyph width before finalizing (documented in redcon.md's Editor section).

episode_summaries.crisis: Changeling infiltration of Starfleet Command — Leyton coup attempt (2372)
episode_summaries.notes: Redcon divergence from DS9 'Homefront'/'Paradise Lost': Odo and the cross-era Voyager EMH expose the real Changeling infiltrator and separately prove that the human Admiral Leyton engineered the invasion scare and coup. Lore was checked after the user's review: Leyton is human, although a Changeling briefly impersonated him; the Founder baseline and nonlethal quantum scan are explicitly alternate-timeline inventions. Pacing revision: the original mandatory long hook could not fit a 5s teaser naturally. After user feedback, the approved final uses a shortened 19-word hook at TTS speed 1.15 with no post-atempo and retimes scene 1 to 6.71s; this episode intentionally omits the usual 'from the link in bio' hook phrase as a one-off user-approved pacing override. Title remains 3s silent, subtitles contain 74 words, and the exact CTA asset remains clip 8.

episode_summaries.crisis: USS Enterprise-C does not return through the temporal rift — Narendra III / "Yesterday's Enterprise" (2366)
episode_summaries.notes: User-requested continuous graphic banner overlay (existing branding asset worf-redcon-cta-banner.png, top-center, ~650px/60% of canvas width) spanning clips 4-5 (canon reminder + crew assembled) as one continuous element across the cut — fade-in 0.3s at clip 4 start, fade-out 0.3s at clip 5 end, no fade at the mid-cut. Incident caught before publish: the mandatory title card text (clip 2, ASS-rendered per this format's Editor section, not tools/overlays.py) was skipped on the first assembly pass because the manager's instruction to the Editor to skip reading rules/formats/redcon.md (intended only for universal subtitle/overlay styling) was too broad and also caused it to skip this format's own mandatory title-card convention. Fixed via a second Editor pass: title_lines reflowed from the storyboard's unbalanced 4-entry split into 4 balanced short lines ("WHAT IF" / "THANKS TO YOU" / "THE ENTERPRISE-C" / "NEVER WENT HOME"), font size measured against Montserrat-Black.ttf and stepped down from fs104 to fs88 to fit the 1080px frame width (max line 955px) — same reflow failure pattern as episode 3, now happening on a fresh run despite the documented rule, worth flagging in redcon.md's Editor section if it recurs a third time.
